question: In an adult trauma patient undergoing resuscitation, a urine output of at least 0.5 mL/kg/hour is an accepted indicator of adequate organ perfusion and successful volume replacement.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Urine output ≥0.5 mL/kg/hour is the accepted ATLS threshold in adults for adequate renal (and systemic) perfusion. Outputs below this threshold suggest ongoing haemorrhage or inadequate resuscitation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Urine output ≥0.5 mL/kg/hour in adults (≥1 mL/kg/hour in children) is the standard ATLS target for adequate renal perfusion during trauma resuscitation. It is one of the key end-points for monitoring the response to fluid therapy.
